It is time to retake our homeworld. Even though the planet is not cursed, there are still dangers. Dormant species have been awakened from the bombings. We send down a small recon party. We'll scout the surface, find out what remains of the Great Forge, and establish a safe perimeter. Only then, will we bring down the others. I need volunteers from both tribes.|Bo-Katan Kryze, to the gathered Mandalorians on Nevarro|}} The '''liberation of Mandalore''',{{InsiderCite|222|Jedi Master's Quiz}} also known as the '''conflict on Mandalore''', the '''Battle for Mandalore''',''[[Star Wars: Galaxy of Heroes]]'' '''Showdown on Mandalore''',''[[Star Wars: The Mandalorian Visual Guide]]'' or the '''Last Battle for Mandalore''',[[The Mandalorian – The Graphic Novel of Season 3|''The Mandalorian'' – The Graphic Novel of Season 3]] was a power struggle that occurred during the [[New Republic Era]] when the [[planet]] [[Mandalore]] was reconquered by a [[Mandalorian resistance|resistance]] [[Children of the Watch|group]] of [[Exile (punishment)|exiled]] [[Mandalorian]]s from the [[Moff]] [[Gideon]] and the [[Imperial Remnant]] that continued to control the planet with the secret support of the [[warlord]]s on the [[Shadow Council (Imperial Remnant)|Shadow Council]] after the [[Galactic Civil War|fall]] of the [[Galactic Empire]]. As a result of the battle, the [[Gideon's Imperial remnant|Gideon forces]] was defeated, while the Mandalorians reclaimed their ancestral [[homeworld]] and began to resettle it. ==Prelude== {{Quote|Bo-Katan Kryze is going off to bring other Mandalorians in exile to us so that we may join together once again. [...] Bo-Katan walks both worlds. And she can bring all tribes together. It is time to retake Mandalore.|"The Armorer"|{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 21: The Pirate}}}} The [[Outer Rim Territories|Outer Rim]]''[[Ultimate Star Wars]]'' [[planet]] of [[Mandalore]], the ancestral [[homeworld]] of the legendary{{Databank|death-watch|Death Watch}} [[Mandalorian warrior]]s and their people, became [[Siege of Mandalore|embroiled]] in [[the galaxy]]-wide conflict during the [[Clone Wars]],{{TCW|Old Friends Not Forgotten}} leading to its [[occupation of Mandalore|occupation]] by the [[Galactic Republic]] and its successor state, the [[Galactic Empire]].{{SWCT|set=2020 Base Series 2|cardname=Bo-Katan Kryze}} During the Imperial occupation, however, many of the [[Mandalorian clan|warrior clans]] were united behind [[Lady]] [[Bo-Katan Kryze]], who had formerly ruled Mandalore as [[regent]] until she was removed from power by the Empire.{{Rebels|Heroes of Mandalore}} They were unified under the banner of the [[Mandalorian resistance]],{{Databank|bo-katan-kryze|Bo-Katan Kryze}} which went on to win a [[Mandalorian Civil War (Imperial Era)|civil war]] against the Empire-backed [[Clan Saxon]] and its [[Imperial Super Commando]]s.{{Rebels|Legacy of Mandalore}} Realizing that they could no longer control Mandalore,{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 11: The Heiress}} the Empire carried out the [[Great Purge of Mandalore]],{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 3: The Sin}} which [[Death|killed]] millions of [[Mandalorian]]s, destroyed their [[capital]] [[domed city]] [[Sundari]],{{BOBF|Chapter 5: Return of the Mandalorian}} and wasted the planet.{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 18: The Mines of Mandalore}} After the [[Night of a Thousand Tears]], Kryze attempted to surrender to the Imperial [[Moff]] [[Gideon]] but Gideon instead betrayed Kryze and took the [[Darksaber]], a [[lightsaber]] of the Mandalorians that symbolized their people's [[Mandalore (title)|leadership]]. Any attempts to flee into [[Realspace|space]] were intercepted and shot down by Imperial forces, while those Mandalorians that survived were driven underground in hiding or scattered across the [[galaxy]].{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 6: The Prisoner}} Among the survivors were Kryze and her remaining followers, as well as a [[Religion|sect]] of the [[Children of the Watch]] known as [[the Tribe]],{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 1: The Mandalorian}} who had been cloistered on the [[moon]] of [[Concordia]]. By [[9 ABY]], Kryze and her followers sought to retake Mandalore, while the Tribe believed the planet had been cursed. During this [[time]], Kryze met [[Din Djarin]], a Child of the Watch. Kryze helped Din [[Assault on Moff Gideon's cruiser|rescue]] his [[foundling]] [[Din Grogu|Grogu]] from Moff Gideon, whose [[Gideon's Imperial remnant|remnant forces]] had established operations from a [[Mandalore Imperial base|base on Mandalore]] and [[Hunt for Grogu|hunted]] Grogu in order to experiment on him. Kryze hoped to take back the Darksaber, but Din claimed it instead after defeating Gideon in combat,{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 16: The Rescue}} causing Kryze's followers to abandon her with the [[Mandalorian fleet]]. Following the rescue of Grogu, Djarin had a new goal, to liberate Mandalore.{{ShipsandVehiclesCite|9|Pilots and Crew Members}} Kryze later reunited with Din after he ventured to Mandalore to bathe in the [[Living Waters]] beneath the [[Mines of Mandalore]], where she rescued him, defeating the creature that had captured him, and thereby reclaiming her right to the Darksaber. After reaching the Living Waters together, she encountered a [[mythosaur]]. Moff Gideon was [[Extraction of Moff Gideon|extracted]] from the [[New Republic]] by his [[beskar]]-[[Imperial Armored Commando|armored commandos]], and regrouped with the rest of his forces on Mandalore. Their [[Gideon's TIE/IN interceptor squadron|TIE interceptor squadron]] then [[Bombing of Kryze Castle|destroyed]] [[Kryze Fortress|Kryze Castle]] on [[Kalevala]], prompting Kryze to follow Din back to his [[Mandalorian secret covert|covert]], where she joined the Tribe.{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 19: The Convert}} Kryze shared her encounter with the mythosaur to the Tribe's leader, "[[the Armorer]],"''[[Star Wars: Character Encyclopedia, Updated and Expanded Edition]]'' who, after the [[pirate siege on Nevarro]], interpreted it as an omen that it was time to reclaim Mandalore. The [[Mandalorian Armorer]] believed that Kryze was the one to reunite their people, for Kryze "walked both worlds" of the [[Way of the Mandalore]]. As such, Kryze was sent off to find other [[Exile (punishment)|exiled]] Mandalorians, and was joined in her quest by Din and Grogu. Kryze and Din [[Mission to Plazir-15|ventured]] to [[Plazir-15]], where Kryze's followers had been hired as a [[mercenary]] [[garrison]]. There, Kryze regained her followers and their [[fleet]] after Din publicly returned the Darksaber to her, and brought them back to [[Nevarro]] to unite with the Tribe. This united group of Mandalorians then prepared to reclaim their ancestral homeworld, but were unaware of the Imperial remnant presence there. ==The conflict== ===Ambushing the Mandalorians=== {{Quote|You were a talented people, but your time has passed. However, as you can see, Mandalore will live on in me. [...] Why don't we take your fleet off the board while we still have the element of surprise? Activate the interceptors and bombers. In but a few moments, the Purge of Mandalore will be complete.|Moff Gideon|}} [[File:Attempt_to_retake_Mandalore_MandoS3.png|thumb|left|300px|Gideon confronts the Mandalorians.]] After they departed from Nevarro, the Mandalorian fleet arrived in orbit of Mandalore, from where a [[scout]] party led by Bo-Katan Kryze was sent ahead to survey the planet and establish a safe perimeter for the rest of the Mandalorians to land. There, they were met by a group of [[Mandalorian survivors|surviving Mandalorians]] who had remained hidden underground on the planet. Their [[Unidentified Mandalorian captain|captain]] reaffirmed their allegiance to Kryze, their former ruler, and took the party to the [[Great Forge]]. However, at the ruins of the Great Forge, the Mandalorians were unexpectedly ambushed by Imperial Armored Commandos, who lured the Mandalorian warriors back to their secret base. There, Din was captured by Moff Gideon, who revealed himself alive, in a [[Dark Trooper phase 4|fourth-generation design Dark Trooper]] suit of [[armor]], and in command of Imperial operations on the planet. [[Paz Vizsla]] sacrificed himself to buy time for the other Mandalorians to escape the base with Kryze. The warrior was ultimately killed by three [[Praetorian Guard|Imperial Praetorian Guard]]s, who had been sent by the secret [[Shadow Council (Imperial Remnant)|Shadow Council]] to reinforce Gideon and his forces. ===Charging into the base=== Din killed his captors, however, and reunited with Grogu. As they made their way through the base, Din discovered that Gideon had been [[cloning]] himself, he sabotaged and destroyed the [[Gideon's clones|clones]]. Din and Gideon then fought each other at the base's command center as Kryze, wielding the Darksaber, led her Mandalorians in a charge against the Imperial Armored Commandos. During the fighting, Kryze relieved Din, who rescued Grogu from the Praetorian Guards. Din and Kryze then fought Gideon together. Meanwhile [[Axe Woves]] regrouped with the Mandalorian fleet's [[Gideon's light cruiser|light cruiser]] [[flagship]] and sent its personnel down to Mandalore as the fleet came under attack from Gideon's [[TIE/IN interceptor|TIE interceptor]] and [[TIE/sa tactical bomber|bomber]] [[squadron]]. ===Final actions=== As the burning [[Starship|ship]] descended toward the surface of Mandalore, Woves navigated it toward the Imperial base and evacuated the ship just before it crashed into the base. Gideon and his remaining forces were caught in the resulting explosion, while Grogu [[Force barrier|protected]] Din and Kryze with [[the Force]]. ==Aftermath== ===Liberation of Mandalore=== {{Quote|For Mandalore!|Axe Woves and the Mandalorians' chant|}} In the wake of the battle, the surviving Mandalorians traveled to the Living Waters for the the ceremonial induction of [[Ragnar Vizsla]] into the Tribe. Following Ragnar's induction, Din Djarin publicly adopted Grogu as his son and apprentice, and the foundling took the name Din Grogu. "The Armorer" told Din Djarin that it was time for them to leave Mandalore so that he could teach Grogu. Soon after, the Mandalorians witnessed Bo-Katan Kryze relight the Great Forge. With Mandalore retaken and Grogu adopted as his son and apprentice, Din traveled to the [[Adelphi Base]], where he offered himself as an independent contractor for the New Republic to [[Captain]] [[Carson Teva]] to hunt down Imperial remnants, citing his [[Standard year|years]] of experience as a [[bounty hunter]]. Din and Grogu then returned to Nevarro, where they set up home at a cabin given to them by [[High Magistrate]]{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 17: The Apostate}} [[Greef Karga]]. ===New Republic reaction=== {{Quote|There is no proof of any coordination between the scattered and dwindling number of Imperial forces.''"
"''What about the conflict on Mandalore?''"
"''Exactly my point. Gideon was a warlord acting on his own.|Hamato Xiono and Carson Teva, on the threat of the Imperial Remnant|{{Ahsoka|Part Seven: Dreams and Madness}}}} [[File:ThreepioTevaSyndullaCourt-Ahsoka-PartSeven.png|275px|thumb|right|Carson Teva mentioned the conflict on Mandalore during Hera Syndulla's trial.]] During [[General]] [[Hera Syndulla]]'s admonishing session at [[Coruscant]] for disobeying the orders of the [[New Republic Senate]] to ignore the [[Eye of Sion|attempts]] of [[Morgan Elsbeth's forces]] to bring [[Grand Admiral]] [[Mitth'raw'nuruodo|Thrawn]] from [[Far galaxy|another galaxy]], Teva suggested the reconquest of Mandalore as an example of how there had been coordination among the scattered and dwindling [[Imperial holdouts]], but [[Senator]] [[Hamato Xiono]] dismissed Teva's intervention due to feeling that Gideon had been a [[warlord]] acting on his own, so the conflict was not proof of a greater conspiracy posing a threat immediately for the Republic. ==Behind the scenes== The mission to retake Mandalore was first mentioned in the [[The Mandalorian Season Two|Season Two]] episode of [[Jon Favreau]]'s television series ''[[Star Wars: The Mandalorian]]'' titled "[[Chapter 11: The Heiress]]," written by Favreau and directed by [[Bryce Dallas Howard]]. The actual reconquest of Mandalore appeared in the [[The Mandalorian Season Three|Season Three]] episodes "[[Chapter 23: The Spies]]" and "[[Chapter 24: The Return]]," written by Favreau and [[Dave
